name: expense_add
description: Record one expense. The amount is the gross amount on the receipt; vat_rate splits it into net and VAT. If no category is given, the stored category rules are matched against the merchant. Amounts are integer minor units in the expense's own currency.

arguments.name: amount
arguments.desc: Gross amount on the receipt, in major units, e.g. 12.34

arguments.name: currency
arguments.desc: ISO code, default EUR

arguments.name: category
arguments.desc: Category, e.g. software, travel, office. Omit to let the category rules decide

arguments.name: merchant
arguments.desc: Who was paid, e.g. Adobe

arguments.name: date
arguments.desc: ISO date YYYY-MM-DD, default today

arguments.name: project
arguments.desc: Project or client this belongs to

arguments.name: receipt_path
arguments.desc: Absolute path to the receipt file; it is checked and hashed

arguments.name: billable
arguments.desc: Rebillable to the client, default false

arguments.name: vat_rate
arguments.desc: VAT percent already included in amount

name: expense_list
description: List expenses in a date range, optionally filtered by project, category or billable flag. Totals are grouped by currency and never mixed.

arguments.name: from
arguments.desc: ISO date, inclusive

arguments.name: to
arguments.desc: ISO date, inclusive

name: expense_update
description: Change any field of a stored expense by id. Only the fields you pass are changed.

arguments.name: id
arguments.desc: Expense id from expense_add or expense_list

arguments.name: rebilled
arguments.desc: false clears the rebilled marker so the expense can be billed again

name: expense_delete
description: Delete one expense by id. The receipt file itself is left on disk.

name: receipt_attach
description: Attach a receipt file to a stored expense. The file must exist; its path and sha256 are stored so a later audit can prove the file has not changed.

arguments.name: path
arguments.desc: Path to the receipt file

name: category_rules
description: Replace the merchant-to-category rules, or call with no rules to list them. Each match is tried as a case-insensitive regular expression, and as a plain substring if it is not valid regex. The first matching rule wins, and rules are applied by expense_add when no category is given.

arguments.name: rules
arguments.desc: The full rule list. Omit to list the current rules

name: expense_summary
description: Totals for a date range grouped by category, project, month or merchant. Every group is reported per currency with the gross, the net and the VAT; currencies are never added together.

arguments.name: from
arguments.desc: ISO date, inclusive

arguments.name: to
arguments.desc: ISO date, inclusive

arguments.name: group_by
arguments.desc: How to group the totals

name: mileage_add
description: Record a business trip as an expense. Money is distance x rate, using the built-in rate table (PL 1.15 PLN/km, UK 0.45 GBP/mile, US 0.70 USD/mile, EU 0.30 EUR/km) unless you pass your own rate. Give either km or miles.

arguments.name: km
arguments.desc: Distance in kilometres

arguments.name: miles
arguments.desc: Distance in miles

arguments.name: date
arguments.desc: ISO date, default today

arguments.name: purpose
arguments.desc: Why the trip was made, e.g. client meeting in Krakow

arguments.name: region
arguments.desc: Which rate to use. Default US for miles, EU for km

arguments.name: rate_per_km
arguments.desc: Your own rate per supplied unit, overriding the table

arguments.name: currency
arguments.desc: Currency for your own rate, default the region currency

name: expense_export
description: Write the expenses in a date range to a csv, xlsx or json file and return its path. Nothing partial is ever written: if a limit is hit the file is not created at all.

arguments.name: from
arguments.desc: ISO date, inclusive

arguments.name: to
arguments.desc: ISO date, inclusive

arguments.name: path
arguments.desc: Where to write it. Default is the server data directory

name: expense_to_invoice
description: Turn the unbilled billable expenses of one project into invoice line items shaped exactly as invoice_create expects: description, quantity, unit_price, tax_rate. unit_price is the net amount, tax_rate is the VAT rate, so the invoice recomputes the same tax. Line items are grouped per currency because one invoice carries one currency. The expenses are marked as rebilled.

arguments.name: project
arguments.desc: Project or client to rebill

arguments.name: from
arguments.desc: ISO date, inclusive

arguments.name: to
arguments.desc: ISO date, inclusive

arguments.name: markup_percent
arguments.desc: Percent added to each net amount. Pro

arguments.name: include_rebilled
arguments.desc: Include expenses already marked as rebilled, default false

arguments.name: mark_rebilled
arguments.desc: Mark the expenses as rebilled, default true

name: license_status
description: Show whether this server runs in free or Pro mode and where to upgrade.

name: license_activate
description: Activate a Pro license key (format MCPL1.xxx.yyy). Verified offline and saved locally.

arguments.name: key
arguments.desc: License key from the checkout confirmation page
